heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium image generation, multimodal editing, and synchronized audio-video creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected split composition with the media block on the left as a layered gallery panel: one large hero still, two smaller stacked preview cards, and a thin prompt-to-output strip. Keep the right side text-heavy with a strong orange CTA and a prominent logo trust band under the subheadline. Add decorative gradient orbs and subtle grid lines behind the media block. Introduce alternating feature sections with one dark charcoal section for Seedance 1.5 Pro, and reserve light sections for Seedream 4.5 and supporting proof. The overall feel should be premium, editorial, and gallery-led rather than dashboard-like.

blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation for Creative Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Built for creative directors, video producers, art directors, and marketing teams.

sections.backgroundTreatment: bold solid color with abstract-shape overlays and floating preview chips
sections.designNote: Content-first but dynamic: answer what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Use a premium split hero with a large AI content showcase on the right: layered image and video mockups, prompt-to-output preview, and a compact benefits stack. Keep the CTA as a solid orange button labeled 'Get started'.

Place trust early as a logo-first marquee with 3-6 recognisable logos. If logos cannot be supplied, use a tight metric strip, but prefer logo dominance. Keep it visually light to reset the orange hero and reinforce enterprise confidence.

Combine both product sections into a strong alternating story. First block: Seedream 4.5 as a spotlight panel with a preview on one side and a feature grid on the other, emphasizing text-to-image, editing, composition, and typography. Second block: Seedance 1.5 Pro in a dark contrast panel with motion preview emphasis and fewer, sharper feature callouts focused on text-to-video, audio-visual sync, lip-sync, and cinematic control. Because there are 5+ features, use spotlight-plus-grid rather than a plain card list.

Make this a dark credibility bridge if included conceptually, but keep it minimal because the provided content does not supply a strong 'why us' narrative. Use a 3-4 card grid for enterprise confidence cues such as guided evaluation, demo support, simplified procurement, and creative workflow fit. Maintain contrast after the product section and before pricing.

Use two premium pricing cards with the video product slightly emphasized if needed, but keep the section lead-generation oriented rather than self-serve. Avoid overwhelming detail; present the plans as decision anchors with clear include lists and a single solid 'Get started' CTA on each card.

Since there are 4+ testimonials, use a carousel. Keep it concise and profession-led: creative director, video producer, art director, marketing manager, creative lead. This should feel like peer validation after pricing, not a long quote wall.

End with a high-contrast centered conversion card. Make the ask simple and commitment-light. Keep the only button label as 'Get started', full-width on mobile, solid accent orange at 100% opacity, and visually dominant over the dark background.
Use as a small footer-adjacent credibility strip only if needed, not as a major news module. Keep it quiet and utility-like so the page ends cleanly after the strong CTA.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium creative studio meets enterprise AI lab: bold orange leadership, clean white breathing room, deep charcoal contrast zones, logo-first trust, and immersive gallery storytelling with interactive media previews.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a polished gallery-first approach with a mixed media strip containing video thumbnails, image samples, prompt-to-output previews, and cinematic motion stills. The hero should feature an AI content showcase panel with layered mockups, floating chips, and a prominent logo trust band. Logos must be the dominant trust signal, with a marquee row of recognizable customer or ecosystem logos above the fold. Use SVG for iconography and logos, PNG for UI/product previews, and JPEG for large hero or gallery visuals.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width split hero with brand/logo anchor, large centered headline, short supporting copy, and a compact benefits list using checkmark bullets; content is text-first with no prominent media in the hero.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column narrative flow with stacked sections separated by strong vertical spacing; hero leads into a form block, then feature-rich content sections, with limited visual interruption and a linear conversion path.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-first white cards with subtle borders/shadows, rounded corners, and dense informational content; cards prioritize readability over decoration and likely support simple hover elevation rather than heavy effects.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA-led conversion pattern with a dominant hero action and secondary section-specific request/demo CTAs; buttons are concise, business-focused, and repeated at section boundaries to reduce friction.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the reference layout; pricing is absent or deferred, implying a lead-generation-first pattern rather than self-serve purchase flow.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference; likely a minimal or standard utility footer outside the captured scope.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo-led header treatment with minimal hero media; product imagery is not central, suggesting a text-and-forms presentation with optional iconography for feature reinforcement.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Product sections are structured as branded modules with a label, headline, description, CTA, and a stacked feature list; each module can function independently and is suitable for repeating comparison-style content.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture form placed immediately after the hero, using a card container and hidden tracking fields; form is designed for short-path conversion with enterprise lead qualification rather than transactional checkout.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Mostly static presentation with potential light transitions only; no explicit motion system is indicated in the reference HTML.

If media is added, keep it supportive and secondary to the message.

designStrategy.reasoning: This is a lead-generation landing page for a category-style AI content solution aimed at professional creators, so the strategy should prioritize clarity, credibility, and demo intent rather than direct purchase. The audience is solution-aware and evaluating capabilities, which makes a product-led narrative appropriate: show what Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro do, then prove it with real output examples, testimonials, and a clear quote/demo path. Because the visitor trusts logos most, logo-led proof should be the dominant trust signal, with the design making room for recognizable brand validation before deeper persuasion. A split hero is the best fit because it supports a strong headline, concise supporting copy, and a primary CTA while leaving space for structured trust or gallery content. Balanced section density keeps the page professional and information-rich without feeling dense or cluttered, and medium CTA aggression supports lead capture without appearing overly salesy.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
